coverage: Unmodified stock servicemanager launched with explicit userspace Shield policy and service-context mapping; all three peers confirm their distinct kernel-held labels
Real IServiceManager registration, lookup from another process, BBinder call returning 42, and service listing
A separate denied label cannot add, find or list services
Stock registration callback and unregister succeed; callback arrives as one-way with Linux sender-PID semantics
Three numbered one-way transactions are observed in order before a synchronous call
Owner exit triggers stock manager death handling; lookup then returns no service and the existing proxy returns DEAD_OBJECT
All peers exit zero; only the fixture-owned manager is killed and reaped with status 137
Native one-way queues retain bounds through delivered messages, serialize per object, permit other objects and synchronous calls, and release resources on revoke/close/drop
Binder one-way completion, dispatch during a synchronous request, failed usercopy cleanup, reply rejection and buffer-controlled serialization
Existing Bionic, stock libbinder object/death and stock libselinux authorization regressions pass
limitations: Explicit userspace integration fixture; no persistent Android manager, full Android boot, framework/Zygote startup or APK execution claim
Nested synchronous calls, FD/buffer transfer, weak promotion, automatic worker-pool growth, security-context records and priority inheritance remain unsupported
Shield service authorization does not implement full SELinux binary policy, VFS MAC, Unix credentials or Binder call/transfer classes
Endpoint lifetime still follows the open-file description, including foreign inherited references
Kernel release build precedes test-only assertion and comment cleanup; production logic is unchanged
